# Readme Studio

> Design animated, self-updating GitHub READMEs (profile READMEs and project/repository READMEs) as a JSON config. A GitHub Action (`DavidNiessen/readme-studio@v1`) renders every widget to dark/light SVG (or GIF), pushes the images to an asset branch and rewrites README.md on a schedule.

Everything is driven by one file, `readme.config.json` (schema: https://readme.niessen.dev/schema.json). An agent can create it, validate it, render it offline and hand the user a link to fine-tune it visually.

## Workflow for agents

1. Get the CLI (self-contained bundle, no install):
   `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DavidNiessen/readme-studio ~/.cache/readme-studio`
   then `node ~/.cache/readme-studio/packages/engine/dist/cli.mjs <command>`.
2. Discover: `widgets --json [--kind profile|project]`, `presets --json`, `themes --json`, `schema`.
3. Start: `init --login <user> [--kind project --repo owner/name --npm <pkg>] [--preset <id>] --workflow`
   writes readme.config.json and .github/workflows/readme-studio.yml in the current directory.
4. Edit readme.config.json (layout rows → blocks with `type`, `id`, `options`; theme; profile/project).
5. Check: `validate --json` (repairs are reported as warnings), then `build --mock --out /tmp/rs` renders every asset and README.md offline (open preview.html to look at it).
6. Hand off: `link` prints a https://readme.niessen.dev/ URL that opens the design in the visual studio.
   A committed config can also be opened with https://readme.niessen.dev/#/studio?repo=owner/name.
7. Commit readme.config.json, README.md (from the build) and the workflow; the user enables
   Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → Read and write, and runs the "Readme Studio" workflow once.

## Config essentials

- `kind`: "profile" (the <login>/<login> repository) or "project" (any public repository; set `project.repo`).
- `profile`: `login` (whose data is fetched), `location` (city, latitude, longitude, timezone) and `links`. `project`: `repo` and `packages` (npm, pypi, crates).
- Names, roles, bios, taglines and logos are options of the widgets that show them (hero `title`/`roles`, about `name`/`bio`, project-hero `title`/`tagline`/`emblem`) and default to the GitHub profile or repository.
- `layout`: array of rows `{ align, blocks: [{ id, type, options, hidden?, link? }] }`. Blocks in one row sit side by side (use half-width widgets in pairs). `id` becomes the image file name.
- `theme`: `preset` (palette), `font`, `headingFont`, `radius`, `border`, `texture` (dots|grid|lines|none), `motion` (full|subtle|off), `surface`, optional `accent` to generate a palette.
- `media`: the media library, `[{ id, name, data }]` with `data` a base64 PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP data URI (at most 200,000 characters; keep images near 256 px). Icon options use one as `media:<id>`; replacing its `data` updates every widget using it.
- `output`: `branch` (asset branch, default "readme-studio"), `modes` (["dark","light"]), `schedule` (cron), `repository`.
- Free text accepts placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}.
- Icon options take a line icon (`rocket`, `database`, `git-branch`), a brand (`rust`, `docker`, `figma`) or `media:<id>` for an image in the design's media library. llms-full.txt lists every id.
- Unknown widgets are skipped and invalid values repaired; `validate` lists every repair.

## Palettes

- `crimson`: Crimson. Signal red on graphite. The original command-center look.
- `github`: GitHub. Native GitHub surfaces with the familiar green graph.
- `paper`: Paper. Warm off-white stock and ink-blue accents. Editorial and calm.
- `mono`: Monochrome. Pure greyscale. Lets typography and motion do the talking.
- `ember`: Ember. Glowing orange on charcoal, like a forge at night.
- `amber`: Amber CRT. Phosphor amber, scanlines optional. Retro terminal energy.
- `forest`: Forest. Moss and canopy greens with soft, earthy neutrals.
- `ocean`: Ocean. Deep navy with a sharp cyan current.
- `nord`: Nord. Arctic, north-bluish calm from the Nord palette.
- `gruvbox`: Gruvbox. Retro groove: warm, high-legibility contrast.
- `solarized`: Solarized. Precision colours for machines and people.
- `tokyo`: Tokyo Night. Neon-lit city blues after the last train.
- `dracula`: Dracula. The classic dark theme with candy accents.
- `mocha`: Catppuccin. Soothing pastels: Mocha by night, Latte by day.
- `rose`: Rosé. Soho vibes: muted roses, pine and gold.
- `ultraviolet`: Ultraviolet. Electric violet and lime for the loud ones.
- `sakura`: Sakura. Cherry-blossom pink on soft plum.

## Fonts

`jetbrains-mono`, `ibm-plex-mono`, `fira-code`, `geist-mono`, `space-mono`, `source-code-pro`, `inter`, `geist-sans`, `space-grotesk`, `manrope`, `fraunces`, `ibm-plex-serif`

## Presets

- `command-center` (profile): Command Center. Everything, animated: hero, live stats, a 3D skyline, departure board and project cards. The full show.
- `minimal-paper` (profile): Minimal Paper. Editorial serif headlines on warm paper. Quiet motion, generous whitespace, all signal.
- `terminal` (profile): Terminal. Amber phosphor and a shell that types itself. For people who live in tmux.
- `data-nerd` (profile): Data Nerd. Every number GitHub knows about you, charted: trends, year in review, rhythms and a harvest loop.
- `portfolio` (profile): Designer Portfolio. A soft, rounded showcase: statement banner, selected work, skills and a contact card.
- `maintainer` (profile): Open Source Maintainer. Native GitHub colours. Leads with your repositories, releases and the green graph.
- `student` (profile): Student. Fresh and friendly: about, quick facts, an education timeline, skills you're building and today's quote.
- `retro-arcade` (profile): Retro Arcade. Warm gruvbox colours, a glitching title and a spinning skyline in chunky mono.
- `nordic` (profile): Nordic Calm. Arctic blues, serif headlines and slow, deliberate motion. Clocks, weather and long-form writing.
- `one-card` (profile): One Card. Monochrome and minimal: a headline, your links and one streak card. Nothing else.
- `live-wire` (profile): Live Wire. Electric violet on ink. A marquee banner, the harvester, a trend line and rotating quotes.
- `writer` (profile): Writer. For developers who blog: an intro in real markdown, your latest posts and a quote to end on.
- `oss-library` (project): Open-Source Library. The full treatment for a published package: hero, live shields, install terminal, usage, stars and the people who built it.
- `cli-tool` (project): CLI Tool. Terminal-first: amber phosphor, a typed install, a usage snippet and the commit pulse of the project.
- `product-launch` (project): Product Launch. Bold and visual for apps and frameworks: statement banner, feature grid, roadmap progress and a sponsor card.
- `python-package` (project): Python Package. Calm Nord palette for a PyPI package: pip install, a code sample, releases and repository vitals.
- `minimal-oss` (project): Minimal OSS. Monochrome and quiet: a title, a row of shields, real markdown docs and nothing that shouts.
- `maintainers-dashboard` (project): Maintainer's Dashboard. Everything a maintainer watches, at a glance: stats, health, downloads, star growth, commit rhythm and milestones.

## Widgets (54)

- `hero` (profile, full): Hero banner. Your name drawn on stroke by stroke, a typewriter cycling through your roles and an orbiting emblem.
- `banner` (profile + project, full): Statement banner. A big typographic statement with a subline, brought to life by a gradient sweep, an outline draw-on, a letter-by-letter rise or a marquee.
- `project-hero` (project, full): Project hero. Your project's name drawn on, its tagline, version, install command and headline numbers over an ambient glow.
- `socials` (profile + project, full): Social pills. One animated, clickable pill per profile link. Each is its own image so every link works.
- `terminal` (profile, full): Terminal. A shell session that types out commands about you, with live placeholders, syntax colours and a tmux-style status bar.
- `stack` (profile + project, full): Tech stack orbit. Your tools as a little solar system: up to three rings of brand icons orbiting a centre emblem.
- `about` (profile, full): About card. A typographic introduction: monogram, name and pronouns, your roles, a short bio and chips for where you work and live.
- `facts` (profile + project, full): Quick facts. A tidy key-value list of things worth knowing about you, revealed row by row, in one or two columns.
- `badges` (profile + project, full): Badges. A row of shields-style badges drawn right in the image, no third-party service, wrapping neatly across lines.
- `skills` (profile, full): Skill meters. Your strongest tools as filling bars, segmented blocks or radial gauges, each with its icon and level.
- `timeline` (profile, full): Timeline. Experience and education on a vertical rail whose nodes light up one after another, with a live pulse on what you do now.
- `contact` (profile + project, full): Contact card. A “let's work together” card with your availability, a short pitch and up to three call-to-action buttons.
- `clock` (profile + project, half): Local time. A live clock for your time zone that keeps ticking after the build, with your city, UTC offset and today's daylight band.
- `shields` (project, full): Shields. Shield-style badges for version, licence, build status, stars, downloads and more, each its own image linking to the right page.
- `contributors` (project, full): Contributor wall. Everyone who has committed to the project as a wall of avatars that pop in one by one, top contributors first.
- `support` (profile + project, full): Support & sponsor. A warm call to action for sponsors: headline, a short pitch, up to three drawn buttons (GitHub Sponsors, Ko-fi, Open Collective, …) and a beating heart.
- `stats` (profile, full): Stats board. Rolling odometer counters for your key numbers, with an optional year-progress ring.
- `languages` (profile + project, half): Top languages. Your most used languages by bytes of code, as an animated donut, bar list or stacked bar.
- `trophies` (profile, half): Achievements. Hexagonal trophies that unlock in three tiers as your streaks, stars and years on GitHub grow.
- `streak` (profile, full): Streak card. Current streak in a burning ring, flanked by your longest run and total contributions, each with its date range.
- `donut` (profile + project, half): Language donut. Your languages as a donut that draws itself in, with the top language in the centre and a percentage legend.
- `year` (profile, full): Year in review. Your year, wrapped: total contributions, busiest month, best day, favourite weekday and more, over a monthly bar chart.
- `followers` (profile, half): Follower milestone. Your follower count on a rolling counter with a progress bar towards the next milestone.
- `repo-stats` (project, full): Repository stats. Rolling counters for stars, forks, issues, pull requests and contributors, each with a tiny trend, plus an issue-health ring.
- `repo-health` (project, half): Repository vitals. A compact health check: build status with a live pulse, last commit, latest release, issue and pull request balance, and the licence.
- `downloads` (project, half): Package downloads. Weekly, monthly or all-time downloads from npm, PyPI or crates.io on a rolling counter, with a year-long sparkline and the month-on-month trend.
- `contrib` (profile, full): Contribution graph. Your last 12 months as an animated heatmap with a scanning beam, best-day callout and weekly totals.
- `pulse` (profile, full): Heartbeat. Your recent contributions drawn as an ECG trace, one heartbeat per day, with a glowing pulse running along it.
- `skyline` (profile, full): 3D skyline. Your last 12 months as an isometric city of contribution towers, slowly turning in an animated GIF.
- `rhythm` (profile, half): Coding rhythm. A 24-hour radial clock of when you commit, with your chronotype and busiest weekday.
- `journey` (profile, full): Journey timeline. Your years on GitHub as a timeline: contributions per year above the axis, repositories you started below.
- `board` (profile, full): Departure board. Your latest public GitHub activity on a split-flap departure board that clatters into place.
- `area` (profile, full): Contribution trend. Weekly contributions as a smooth area chart that draws itself on, with your average and peak week marked.
- `weekdays` (profile, half): Weekday rhythm. Contributions per day of the week as rising bars, with your busiest day lit up.
- `harvest` (profile, full): Contribution harvester. A scanner drone glides over your contribution graph, harvesting every lit cell into a running tally before the grid regrows.
- `star-history` (project, full): Star history. Cumulative stars over time as a chart that draws itself on, with milestone flags and the stars gained this month.
- `commit-activity` (project, full): Commit activity. A year of weekly commits as growing bars, a heat strip or a line, with the busiest week called out and the latest commit underneath.
- `now` (profile, full): Now building. Spotlights the project you are pushing to right now, with an animated git graph and the last 30 days of activity.
- `project` (profile, half): Project card. One repository as a polished card with its description, language and stars, framed by a running accent light.
- `repos` (profile, full): Top repositories. Your best or most recently pushed repositories with descriptions, languages and rolling star counters.
- `releases` (profile + project, half): Latest releases. A timeline of the versions you shipped most recently, with tag pills, repositories and how long ago each landed.
- `posts` (profile + project, full): Latest posts. The newest articles from your blog's RSS or Atom feed, with dates and short summaries, refreshed on every build.
- `changelog` (project, full): Changelog. Your latest releases on a timeline: version pills, dates, a line or two of release notes and a pulsing marker on the newest one.
- `roadmap` (project, full): Roadmap. Milestones as progress rows with status chips, issue counts and due dates, from GitHub milestones or a list you write.
- `today` (profile + project, half): Today. Today at a glance: the date, the moon phase, local weather, the year so far and a quote of the day.
- `quote` (profile + project, full): Quote. A large typographic quote with attribution; add several and it cross-fades through them on a loop.
- `markdown` (profile + project, full): Markdown text. Free-form Markdown or HTML written straight into your README, with live placeholders like {name} and {followers}.
- `install` (project, full): Install command. A terminal that types your install command, cycling through package-manager tabs, with a copy button and an optional quick-start line.
- `code` (project, full): Code snippet. A syntax-highlighted code card with a file tab, line numbers, highlighted lines and a line-by-line reveal: perfect for a usage example.
- `features` (project, full): Feature grid. Your project's highlights as a two- or three-column grid of icon tiles, titles and short descriptions, revealed one by one.
- `toc` (profile + project, full): Table of contents. A markdown table of contents with links to your README's sections, numbered or bulleted, with optional sub-entries.
- `divider` (profile + project, full): Divider. A thin animated separator between sections: comet, pulse, wave, dashes or a fading line.
- `footer` (profile + project, full): Footer. Rolling waves, a date barcode and a build stamp that proves the profile is alive.
- `heading` (profile + project, full): Section heading. A slim section title with an eyebrow label and an animated hairline, for giving your README a clear structure.

Full option reference: https://readme.niessen.dev/llms-full.txt · JSON: https://readme.niessen.dev/widgets.json, https://readme.niessen.dev/presets.json

## Widget options

### hero

Hero banner: Your name drawn on stroke by stroke, a typewriter cycling through your roles and an orbiting emblem.
Category Header · output svg · width full · for profile READMEs

- `title` (text) · default ""
- `roles` (tags) · default ["Software Engineer","Open-source tinkerer","Coffee-driven developer"] · Cycled by the typewriter. Other widgets and the {role} placeholder use the first.
- `typewriter` (toggle) · default true · Cycles through the roles above.
- `greeting` (toggle) · default true · Time-of-day greeting, date and moon phase.
- `emblem` (icon) · default "github"
- `emblemStyle` (segmented: orbit | plain | none) · default "orbit"
- `glitch` (toggle) · default true
- `scanline` (toggle) · default true
- `glow` (toggle) · default true

### banner

Statement banner: A big typographic statement with a subline, brought to life by a gradient sweep, an outline draw-on, a letter-by-letter rise or a marquee.
Category Header · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs

- `headline` (text) · default "Crafting calm, fast software." · Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}
- `subline` (text) · default "Developer tools, typed APIs and small interfaces that feel good to use."
- `effect` (select: gradient | outline | rise | marquee | none) · default "gradient"
- `align` (segmented: left | center) · default "left"
- `height` (segmented: compact | regular | tall) · default "regular"
- `glow` (toggle) · default true
- `corners` (toggle) · default true · Small registration ticks in the corners.

### project-hero

Project hero: Your project's name drawn on, its tagline, version, install command and headline numbers over an ambient glow.
Category Header · output svg · width full · for project READMEs

- `title` (text) · default ""
- `tagline` (text) · default ""
- `emblem` (icon) · default "" · The project's logo. Without one a monogram tile is drawn.
- `align` (segmented: left | center) · default "left"
- `version` (toggle) · default true · Latest release tag next to the name.
- `install` (text) · default "npm i {npm}" · Shown in a code pill under the tagline. Leave empty to hide. It also stays hidden while a placeholder it uses has no value, such as {npm} without an npm package in the Data tab. Placeholders: {npm} {repo} {project} {version}
- `stats` (toggle) · default true
- `third` (segmented: license | downloads | contributors) · default "license"
- `emblemStyle` (segmented: orbit | plain | none) · default "orbit"
- `scanline` (toggle) · default true
- `glow` (toggle) · default true

### socials

Social pills: One animated, clickable pill per profile link. Each is its own image so every link works.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs · one image per item

- `style` (segmented: pill | compact | icon) · default "pill"
- `iconColor` (segmented: accent | brand | text) · default "accent"
- `runner` (toggle) · default true

### terminal

Terminal: A shell session that types out commands about you, with live placeholders, syntax colours and a tmux-style status bar.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile READMEs

- `title` (text) · default ""
- `prompt` (segmented: arrow | chevron | dollar | percent | gt) · default "arrow"
- `cwd` (text) · default "~"
- `commands` (list) · default [{"cmd":"whoami","output":"{b}{name|lower}{/}{?{m} — {role|lower}?}{?{m} @ {a}{b}{company}?}"},{"cmd":"cat profile.json","output":"{m}{ {a}\"login\"{m}: {s}\"{login}\"{m}{?, {a}\"based\"{m}: {s}\"{city}\"?}{?{m}, {a}\"pronouns\"{m}: {s}\"{pronouns}\"?}{?{m}, {a}\"age\"{m}: {n}{age}?}{m},\n{m}  {a}\"repos\"{m}: {n}{repos}{m}, {a}\"followers\"{m}: {n}{followers}{m}, {a}\"streak\"{m}: {n}{streak}{m}, {a}\"coffee\"{m}: {n}Infinity{m} }"},{"cmd":"uptime","output":"{?{m}up {n}{b}{uptime_days}{/}{m} days  ·  ?}{?{t}{uptime_note}{m}  ·  ?}{m}{year} is {t}{year_pct}%{m} done"},{"cmd":"ls ~/stack","output":"{stack}"}]
  - `cmd` (text) · default "echo hello"
  - `output` (text) · default "hello, {name}!" · One line per row. Colours: {a}accent {m}muted {s}string {n}number {b}bold {/}reset. Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {age} {days_alive} {account_age} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {year_pct} {stack}. Wrap text in {? … ?} to hide it when a placeholder is empty.
- `stack` (tags) · default ["typescript","react","node","python","go","docker","k8s","postgres","aws"]
- `name` (text) · default ""
- `role` (text) · default ""
- `company` (text) · default ""
- `pronouns` (text) · default ""
- `birthday` (text) · default "" · Optional. Gives {age}, {days_alive} and the uptime line.
- `chrome` (toggle) · default true
- `statusBar` (toggle) · default true
- `tab` (text) · default "[{login}] 0:zsh*"
- `status` (text) · default "git:main  ·  {followers} followers  ·  {clock}" · Supports the same placeholders, plus {clock}, {time}, {date} and {tz}.

### stack

Tech stack orbit: Your tools as a little solar system: up to three rings of brand icons orbiting a centre emblem.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs

- `label` (text) · default "tech stack · orbit"
- `emblem` (icon) · default "github"
- `legend` (toggle) · default true · Lists each ring's tools beside the orbit.
- `rings` (list) · default [{"label":"Languages","icons":["typescript","python","go"]},{"label":"Frameworks","icons":["react","nextjs","nodejs","tailwindcss"]},{"label":"Infra & data","icons":["docker","kubernetes","aws","postgresql","githubactions"]}]
  - `label` (text) · default "Tools"
  - `icons` (tags) · default ["git","linux"] · Icon ids such as typescript, react, docker. Inner rings hold fewer icons than outer ones.

### about

About card: A typographic introduction: monogram, name and pronouns, your roles, a short bio and chips for where you work and live.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile READMEs

- `label` (text) · default "about me"
- `name` (text) · default ""
- `pronouns` (text) · default ""
- `roles` (tags) · default []
- `bio` (text) · default "" · Up to five lines; a blank line starts a new paragraph. Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}
- `layout` (segmented: left | center) · default "left"
- `monogram` (toggle) · default true · Your initials in an accent disc.
- `chips` (toggle) · default true · The city comes from the location in the Data tab.
- `company` (text) · default ""
- `extraChips` (tags) · default ["Open to collaborations"]

### facts

Quick facts: A tidy key-value list of things worth knowing about you, revealed row by row, in one or two columns.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs

- `label` (text) · default "quick facts"
- `columns` (segmented: 1 | 2) · default "2"
- `leaders` (toggle) · default true · A dotted line between each key and its value.
- `iconColor` (segmented: accent | brand | muted) · default "accent"
- `items` (list) · default [{"icon":"pin","key":"Based in","value":"{city}"},{"icon":"briefcase","key":"Working on","value":"Developer tooling"},{"icon":"code","key":"Daily drivers","value":"TypeScript, Rust, Go"},{"icon":"book","key":"Learning","value":"Distributed systems"},{"icon":"coffee","key":"Fuelled by","value":"Flat whites"},{"icon":"sparkle","key":"Ask me about","value":"Design systems, CLIs"}]
  - `icon` (icon) · default "sparkle" · A brand icon, or a line glyph such as pin, briefcase, code, book, heart, rocket, globe.
  - `key` (text) · default "Fun fact"
  - `value` (text) · default "" · Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}

### badges

Badges: A row of shields-style badges drawn right in the image, no third-party service, wrapping neatly across lines.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs

- `style` (segmented: flat | pill | outline) · default "flat"
- `colors` (segmented: accent | brand) · default "accent" · Brand uses each icon's own colour; a per-badge colour always wins.
- `caps` (toggle) · default true
- `align` (segmented: left | center) · default "center"
- `shine` (toggle) · default true
- `items` (list) · default [{"icon":"typescript","label":"TypeScript","value":"daily","color":""},{"icon":"rust","label":"Rust","value":"learning","color":""},{"icon":"react","label":"React","value":"since 2017","color":""},{"icon":"docker","label":"Docker","value":"shipping","color":""},{"icon":"users","label":"Followers","value":"{followers}","color":""},{"icon":"star","label":"Stars","value":"{stars}","color":""},{"icon":"flame","label":"Streak","value":"{streak} days","color":""}]
  - `icon` (icon) · default "code" · Brand icon or line glyph; leave empty for none.
  - `label` (text) · default "Label"
  - `value` (text) · default "value" · Optional. Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}
  - `color` (color) · default "" · Empty uses the accent.

### timeline

Timeline: Experience and education on a vertical rail whose nodes light up one after another, with a live pulse on what you do now.
Category Identity · output svg · width full · for profile READMEs

- `label` (text) · default "experience"
- `now` (toggle) · default true · Marks the top entry as what you are doing now.
- `descriptions` (toggle) · default true
- `items` (list) · default [{"period":"2023 — now","title":"Senior Software Engineer","place":"Northwind Labs","description":"Leading the developer platform team: build tooling, CI pipelines and a design system used by forty engineers."},{"period":"2020 — 2023","title":"Full-stack Developer","place":"Lumen & Co.","description":"Shipped a realtime collaborative editor and halved page load times across the product."},{"period":"2016 — 2020","title":"BSc Computer Science","place":"State University","description":"Distributed systems, compilers and far too many hackathons."}]

### contact

- `ornament` (toggle) · default true

### footer

Footer: Rolling waves, a date barcode and a build stamp that proves the profile is alive.
Category Decoration · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs

- `message` (text) · default "rebuilt every night by readme studio"
- `stamp` (toggle) · default true · Date, time, run number and data source.
- `barcode` (toggle) · default true
- `waves` (toggle) · default true
- `credit` (toggle) · default false · A small credit line, and the footer links to Readme Studio. Thank you!

### heading

Section heading: A slim section title with an eyebrow label and an animated hairline, for giving your README a clear structure.
Category Decoration · output svg · width full · for profile and project READMEs

- `eyebrow` (text) · default "01 · selected work"
- `title` (text) · default "Featured projects" · Placeholders: {name} {login} {city} {company} {role} {year} {followers} {stars} {repos} {streak} {contributions} {project} {repo} {tagline} {version} {license} {forks} {contributors} {npm} {pypi} {crate} {owner}
- `icon` (icon) · default "" · Optional; a brand icon or a line glyph (rocket, code, book, star…).
- `align` (segmented: left | center) · default "left"
- `line` (toggle) · default true
- `card` (toggle) · default false · Off blends the heading into the page.

## Icons
